stats.label: Time saved per week with automation

blocks.text: Why Gmail is the center of your sales world

As a B2B sales rep, your inbox is your command center. You likely spend hours every day reading, writing, and organizing emails. If you do this manually, you lose time that could go toward prospecting or closing deals. On a Mac, you have tools that make this faster. You do not need a native app to be efficient. You just need to master the browser interface.

Most reps click around with their mouse. This is slow. Go to Settings, click See all settings, and find the Keyboard shortcuts section in the General tab. Turn them on. Now you can use keys like j and k to move between emails. Use r to reply and a to reply all. This small change saves minutes every hour.
Use Lazur to dictate your follow-ups

Typing long emails is a drain. Hold the fn key on your Mac to start dictation. Speak your thoughts clearly. Lazur puts the text into your draft. You can keep your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on your CRM data. This is better than typing because you can capture your tone and intent without the physical effort of tapping keys.
Manage your inbox with snooze and labels

Your inbox should only contain items that need action today. If an email is for later, snooze it. Hover over the email in your list and click the clock icon. Pick a date. It disappears and comes back when you are ready. Use labels to organize by deal stage or priority. This keeps your view clean.

items: Use labels for different stages of the sales cycle.
Archive emails that do not need a reply to keep the inbox empty.
Create filters to move newsletters or automated reports into folders.
Set up a standard signature with your contact details and calendar link.

blocks.text: Do not let your inbox become a dumping ground. If you leave emails in your inbox for weeks, you will miss follow-ups. Another mistake is using the mouse for everything. Learn the shortcut for sending emails, which is ⌘ + Enter. Use the search bar to find old threads instead of scrolling.
If you are overwhelmed by tabs, use a browser feature to group them. Right-click a tab and select Add tab to new group. You can name it by account name or project.

blocks.text: How to handle high volume outreach

When you send many emails, use templates. Go to Settings, Advanced, and enable Templates. This allows you to save common responses. When you need one, click the three dots in the compose window. Select Templates and choose your saved draft. This keeps your messaging consistent across all your prospects.

Context switching is the enemy of productivity. When you are in Gmail, stay in Gmail. Do not jump to LinkedIn or your CRM unless you have a specific task. Use Lazur to ask questions about your screen. Ask, Where is the snooze button? or How do I create a label? Lazur points to the exact spot. You never have to leave your flow.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native desktop app for Gmail. You can use a browser or a third-party email client.

faq.question: How do I use keyboard shortcuts in Gmail?
faq.answer: You must enable them in Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts. Once enabled, press ? to see the full list.

faq.question: Can Lazur draft emails for me?
faq.answer: Lazur allows you to dictate text directly into your email draft. It does not write the emails for you, but it makes the process faster.

faq.question: How do I avoid losing track of prospects?
faq.answer: Use the snooze feature for follow-ups and labels to categorize your deals by stage.
